items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...for example, at Speck's Moulin Rouge, I remember Kid Thomas would take a break, eat a sandwich. Now, what time was that? [INTERVIEWEE] Oh, I don't know.

ctx.x: Yeah, but not necessarily. Sometimes, maybe before the union, they might have even taken longer breaks at times. I mean, it depends on what would go on. I mean, but on the other hand, they were used to longer hours. I mean, they might start at 8 o'clock in the evening and play until 4 o'clock in the morning, even. And as far as long hours going, when you hear about these taxi dance halls, where they, you know, a dime a dance or a nickel a dance, they might have been in the old days, where they can hardly put…
You would remember more clearly than I, but for example, at Speck's Moulin Rouge, I remember Kid Thomas would take a break, eat a sandwich. Now, what time was that?
